title: Seagate Sees Storage Demand Outpacing Supply as AI and Cloud Drive HDD Growth
excerpt: Seagate Technology (NASDAQ:STX) CFO Gianluca Romano said the hard-disk-drive maker expects demand for data storage to continue outpacing supply, supported by...
content_html:
Key Points

  • Interested in Seagate Technology Holdings PLC? Here are five stocks we like better.

  • Demand is outpacing supply: Seagate expects the HDD upcycle to continue through fiscal 2027, driven by public-cloud spending, enterprise data centers and AI-related applications. Customer purchase orders and long-term agreements already cover much of the next several quarters.

  • HAMR technology is increasing capacity: Seagate targets at least 25% annual exabyte growth over the next two to three years by moving from 30 TB to 40 TB drives and qualifying 50 TB products in roughly a year.

  • Strong cash flow could boost shareholder returns: Pricing remains favorable as supply stays tight, while capital expenditures are expected to remain at 4%–6% of revenue. After reducing debt, Seagate plans to direct more free cash flow toward share repurchases while maintaining dividends.

  • These 5 ETFs Have Raked in Cash This Year—What Do They All Have in Common?

Seagate Technology (NASDAQ:STX) CFO Gianluca Romano said the hard-disk-drive maker expects demand for data storage to continue outpacing supply, supported by public-cloud spending, enterprise demand and emerging artificial intelligence applications.

Speaking at a Citi technology conference, Romano said the current HDD upcycle has been developing for more than three years, with the company reporting improving revenue and profitability over that period. Based on purchase orders already in place, Seagate expects additional improvement through fiscal 2027, he said.

  • Seagate Technology Stock Surges as Earnings Beat Silences AI Doubters

"Demand is growing even faster than what we were thinking," Romano said. "The gap between supply [and] demand is not decreasing, it is actually a little bit increasing."

Technology Transition Drives Exabyte Growth

Seagate is focusing on increasing the amount of storage capacity shipped, measured in exabytes, rather than expanding the number of drive units it produces. Romano reiterated the company's target to grow exabytes at a compound annual rate of at least 25% over the next two to three years.

→ Nasdaq's $100 Million Kraken Bet Prepares It for a Market That Never Closes

  • Which Storage Stock Is Best Positioned to Win the AI Memory War?

The strategy centers on heat-assisted magnetic recording, or HAMR, technology. Seagate is transitioning from 30-terabyte HAMR drives to 40-terabyte products and expects to begin qualifying a 50-terabyte drive in roughly a year, Romano said.
